metadata.title: Sliding Windows Are Not the End: Exploring Full Ranking with Long-Context Large Language Models

problem.statement: Existing listwise passage ranking methods often adopt the sliding window strategy due to limited input length, which is inefficient and incurs redundant API costs.
limitations_of_prior_work: Existing methods for listwise passage ranking rely on a sliding window strategy, which is inefficient due to repetitive and serialized processing, re-evaluating relevant passages multiple times.
The sliding window strategy incurs redundant API costs proportional to the number of inference tokens.
The sequential dependency between windows in the sliding window strategy limits inference parallelization, leading to efficiency bottlenecks.
Existing listwise training methods based on one-pass sliding windows can only guarantee the order of top-ranked passages, failing to produce a full ranking list as a training label.

Standard language modeling loss used in existing methods applies an equal penalty to all passage IDs in the training label, which is problematic for full ranking labels with hundreds of IDs and an imbalance between relevant and irrelevant passages, overshadowing top-ranked passage IDs.

method.name: Fine-tuned Full Ranking Model with Importance-Aware Learning
method.key_idea: Leverages long-context LLMs for full ranking of all passages within a single inference, overcoming the inefficiencies of sliding windows, and proposes a multi-pass sliding window approach for complete label construction and an importance-aware learning objective for effective fine-tuning.

components.name: Multi-pass Sliding Window Approach
components.function: Iteratively generates a full ranking list as a training label by applying the sliding window strategy multiple times to rerank remaining passages until the entire list is constructed, overcoming the limitation of producing only top-ranked passages in a single pass.

components.name: Importance-Aware Learning Objective
components.function: Reweights passage IDs in the label based on their rank position, assigning higher importance to higher-ranked passage IDs during loss calculation to address the imbalance between relevant and irrelevant passages and align with ranking task evaluation.

techniques.name: Multi-pass Sliding Window
techniques.purpose: To generate high-quality full ranking lists for model fine-tuning, ensuring the construction of a complete ranked list beyond just the top-ranked passages.
techniques.details: Employs BM25 to retrieve top-100 candidate passages. In the first pass, a sliding window strategy reranks all 100 passages, yielding the top 10. This iterative process continues until the entire reranked list is constructed.

techniques.name: Importance-Aware Loss ($L_{ia}$)
techniques.purpose: To address the imbalance in full ranking labels where only a few top-ranked passages are relevant, ensuring that higher-ranked passage IDs receive greater weight during loss calculation.
techniques.details: A modified language modeling loss that includes a position-based weight $w_i$ to reweight each passage ID. $w_i = 1 + \frac{1}{\log_2(p_i+1)}$ for passage IDs, and $\alpha$ for non-passage IDs (e.g., '>') where $\alpha < 1$.

methodology.training_data: 1k queries from MS MARCO training set, with teacher labels generated by GPT-4o-mini or GPT-4o using a multi-pass sliding window strategy.

settings: rerank the top-100 passages retrieved by BM25
outputting only the top-10 passage IDs

main_findings.claim: Our fine-tuned full ranking model (RankMistral100) achieves superior performance compared to the sliding window model (RankMistral20) on TREC DL19.
Our fine-tuned full ranking model (RankMistral100) significantly reduces latency compared to the sliding window model on TREC DL19.
Our full ranking model (RankMistral100) outperforms the sliding window model (RankMistral20) in supervised fine-tuning.
main_findings.value: average improvement of about 4 points on TREC and 2 points on BEIR

main_findings.claim: The full ranking strategy achieves significant efficiency improvement on Qwen-2.5.
The full ranking strategy achieves significant efficiency improvement on GPT-4o.
When outputting only the top-10 passage IDs, the full ranking strategy demonstrates a substantial speed-up.
main_findings.comparison: vs. sliding window strategy (3.8 seconds vs 29.9 seconds)

main_findings.claim: The full ranking strategy reduces API costs compared to the sliding window strategy.
In the zero-shot setting, the full ranking strategy generally underperforms the sliding window strategy.
RankMistral100 performs better than RankMistral20 across different numbers of passages (N).

ablation_insights.effect: Enhances ranking effectiveness by making the model focus more on top-ranked passage IDs.
ablation_insights.delta: Both RankMistral20 and RankMistral100 drop about 0.7 points on BEIR Avg after removing $L_{ia}$.

efficiency_results.latency: approximately 4.5s (Full Ranking Model on TREC DL19)
efficiency_results.throughput: Not explicitly stated as a single value.
efficiency_results.memory: Not explicitly stated as a single value.
efficiency_results.comparison: Full Ranking Model latency is approximately 4.5s, while Sliding Window Model latency is approximately 6.5s on TREC DL19. When outputting only top-10 IDs, full ranking takes 3.8 seconds vs. sliding window's 29.9 seconds on Signal dataset.

contributions.description: We conduct a comprehensive study of long-context LLMs for ranking, being the first to investigate their application in ranking tasks.
We reveal that, in a zero-shot setting, full ranking with long-context models is more efficient but less effective compared to the sliding window strategy.
To enhance the effectiveness of full ranking, we propose a complete listwise label construction approach and a novel importance-aware learning objective for fine-tuning the full ranking model.

comparisons.difference: Full ranking eliminates the repetitive and time-consuming sliding window process and reduces redundant passage inference, leading to higher efficiency.
comparisons.evidence: Full Ranking Model latency is approximately 4.5s vs. Sliding Window Model latency is approximately 6.5s on TREC DL19; full ranking reduces API costs by about 50%.

comparisons.difference: Standard language modeling loss applies equal penalties to all passage IDs, while our importance-aware loss reweights passage IDs based on their rank position, giving more attention to higher-ranked IDs.
comparisons.evidence: Both RankMistral20 and RankMistral100 drop about 0.7 points on BEIR Avg after removing $L_{ia}$.

limitations: Due to limited resources, experiments with larger open-source long-context LLMs (e.g., 30B or 70B parameters) could not be conducted.
The efficiency advantage of the full ranking strategy relies on existing long-context LLMs; a specialized long-context LLM for the ranking task was not designed.
future_work: Investigating the impact of model size on the effectiveness and efficiency of the full ranking strategy.
Designing a specialized long-context LLM for the ranking task.

key_terms.definition: An existing listwise ranking method that processes a subset of passages at a time, sliding a window of fixed size and step size across the entire passage list due to limited LLM input length.
A strategy that enables the input of all retrieved passages and the output of the full ranked list in a single step, eliminating the repetitive and time-consuming sliding window process.

An iterative process to generate a full ranking list as a training label, where the sliding window strategy is applied multiple times to rerank remaining passages until the entire list is constructed.

A loss function that includes a position-based weight $w_p$ to reweight the importance of each passage ID in the label, ensuring higher-ranked passage IDs receive more attention during loss calculation.
